Body and hair: athletic build; a jellyfish cut — a short rounded top layer over long straight lower hair with blunt straight bangs; deep ocean-blue hair with a silvery sheen and a single bright ring of shallow lagoon turquoise around the crown.
Hair: her hair is worn exactly as described above — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless the hair above is an updo.
Expression: one brow slightly raised, attentive eyes.
Her element, carried in her design: flerovium: a synthetic superheavy element sitting at the edge of the island of stability, a theory from the 1960s that nuclei whose protons and neutrons fill certain magic numbers should live far longer than their neighbours; first caught in 1998 by firing calcium ions at a plutonium target, and named for the laboratory that made it; its atoms live for seconds, thousands of times longer than those around it, the first sign that the island is near, though no one has yet reached its centre; it sits below carbon, silicon, germanium, tin and lead, and a few atoms showed it to be the most volatile metal of that column.

No crown unless the opening line says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene.
Silhouette: a many-pocketed expedition jacket, a wide-brimmed hat, a cross-body satchel and laced boots — a far-travelling explorer's shape. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: deep ocean blue, shallow lagoon turquoise, sea-foam white, volatile silver sheen.
Exposure (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — the neckline opened down to the sternum with natural cleavage, bare forearms, and bare legs above the boots or through a high slit where the silhouette allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: around 1909, a survey schooner crossing the open ocean in search of an island that appears on only one old chart: a chart table where the dotted outline of the island is circled again and again, a brass sounding machine and long paid-out lead lines, and from the masthead an endless horizon with the faint shadow of an island just rising out of the haze.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: bright warm sunlight with soft sky light bounced from white clouds.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Fl) and atomic number (114) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, armor plates, cape, modern plastic, sci-fi.
